note_sections.t: Return assessment for previously confirmed prostate malignancy alongside a new PSA elevation reaching 8.7 ng/mL.

At age 70, this secondary school teacher first came to clinical attention in late 2023 due to an incidental PSA increase, which subsequently established an ISUP Grade Group 2 adenocarcinoma diagnosis. His biopsy history ultimately registers as Positive. He resides with his unmarried partner and leads a predominantly sedentary routine, punctuated by occasional recreational walks. Lower urinary tract complaints are moderate, scoring 13 on the IPSS questionnaire, driven mainly by nocturia and a diminished urinary stream; he explicitly denies pelvic discomfort or visible blood in the urine. Alcohol intake is abstinent, and he remains a non-smoker. He has undergone six physiotherapy visits recently to address chronic lumbar ache. Persistent daytime somnolence and loud snoring triggered a sleep clinic referral, raising suspicion for obstructive sleep apnoea. He maintains no regular pharmaceutical regimen, harbors no significant comorbidities, and reports zero drug allergies.

On examination, the digital rectal assessment proves unremarkable, revealing a symmetrically enlarged prostate with a smooth, firm texture devoid of palpable nodules or asymmetry. General inspection shows no pallor, lymphadenopathy, or abdominal masses. Cardiorespiratory and abdominal surveys are stable. Vital parameters record a blood pressure of 130/79 mmHg and a heart rate of 66 bpm.
